chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from the one who narrated it, from Abdul Rahman al-Azramy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn (peace be upon them), and they were both seated upon the Safa (mat). So he begged from them, so they said: 'Charity is not permissible except for a painful debt, or a repulsive loss, or abject poverty. So, is there anything from this in you?' He said, 'Yes'. So they gave him. And the man had begged from Abdullah ibn Umar and Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, and they had given him and had not asked him about anything. So he returned to them and said to them, 'What is the matter with you? You did not ask me about what Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn (peace be upon them) asked me?' And he informed them with what they had said. So they said, 'Those two have been fed with the food of knowledge'.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Safa (a mat made of dried leaves or jute)

ai.seo_question: Why did the Imams ask the man about his specific need before giving him charity?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the jurisprudential precision of the Ahl al-Bayt by contrasting their conditional charity with the general generosity of the Sahaba, such as Abdullah ibn Umar. The Imams’ inquiry into whether the man’s need fell under 'painful debt,' 'repulsive loss,' or 'abject poverty' reflects the specific criteria for *Sadaqah* (obligatory charity) distinct from *Sadaqat* (voluntary), ensuring funds are distributed to those truly eligible. Their explanation that they were 'fed with knowledge' underscores the Shia belief that the Imams possess deep, divinely-inspired understanding of legal nuances, moving beyond mere custom to strict adherence to divine law.
